question: Do the roof posts bear on the new slab via turned-down footings, on separate piers, or on existing deck framing?
unblocks: Post layout staking, footing excavation and rebar ahead of the pour, post-base hardware in the framing package, and whether any deck demo or tie-in tasks exist.

choices: New slab with thickened/turned-down footings at each post
Separate poured piers outside the slab
Existing deck framing (a deck exists next to the pavers)

why_it_matters: Post footings must be staked and formed before the slab pours; an existing deck changes demo and bearing entirely.

question: Which fireplace system is being built: manufactured firebox in a framed chase, site-built masonry, or masonry firebox in a framed chase?
unblocks: Footing design and rebar in the slab pour, chase framing package, chimney penetration layout, fireplace procurement lead time, and whether a mason crew is scheduled.

choices: Manufactured wood-burning firebox in a framed chase with Class A pipe (as drawn)
Site-built masonry fireplace and chimney
Masonry firebox with framed chase and Class A pipe
Not yet selected — hold slab pour until chosen

why_it_matters: The fireplace footing pours with the patio slab and sets chase framing and the roof penetration.

question: Who is pulling the building permit for the roof tie-in and wood-burning fireplace?
unblocks: Permit application task ahead of demo, framing and chimney inspection holds, and final inspection before closeout.

choices: Tri-Cities pulls the building permit (roof + fireplace)
Homeowner pulls the permit
No permit is being pulled — confirmed in writing with the homeowner

why_it_matters: The proposal includes permitting but the breakdown carries none; the plan must know whether to carry permit and inspection tasks.

question: Is the 2026-12-21 scheduled start firm, given concrete and framing cannot run mid-December to mid-February?
unblocks: Plan start date, whether demo and slab are pulled ahead of mid-December, and where the 20% outdoor buffer lands.

choices: Placeholder — plan foundation and framing after mid-February 2027
Pull demo and slab ahead to complete before mid-December 2026, frame after mid-February
Dec 21 firm for demo and prep only; concrete and framing after mid-February
Other date — PM will provide

why_it_matters: The whole build is exterior; a December start leaves only demo and prep until mid-February.

question: Which patio footprint governs, and does the slab extend outside the enclosure to the house entry doors?
unblocks: Excavation and slab dimensions, concrete and gravel quantities, and whether an unpriced apron is added to the pour.

choices: Proposal 12.5' x 23.5', enclosure only
Drawing 24' x 12' overall, enclosure only
Drawing 24' x 12' plus apron along the house to the entry doors
Field-measure at layout; PM will confirm

why_it_matters: Excavation, gravel, concrete quantity, and screen-wall layout depend on the governing footprint.

question: Is the porch to have zero electrical (no lights, fan, or GFCI), or will electrical be added before framing closes?
unblocks: Whether rough electrical, an electrical permit, and fixture install tasks enter the graph before sheathing and screen close.

choices: Zero electrical — written acknowledgement obtained from homeowner
Add lights/fan/GFCI by change order before framing closes
Undecided — obtain acknowledgement or priced adds before roof sheathing

why_it_matters: Electrical added after roofing and screening reopens finished work and adds a permit and inspection.

question: Is the knee wall 2 feet tall per the proposal or 3'-4" per the signed drawings?
unblocks: Screen-wall framing and knee-wall material takeoff.

choices: 2' per proposal
3'-4" per drawings

why_it_matters: Knee-wall height sets wall framing, siding quantity, and screen bay height.

question: Are the brick chimney exterior and the brick corner pier shown in the drawings contracted work?
unblocks: Whether a masonry crew and pier footing are scheduled and whether chase cladding is brick or the priced veneer.

choices: Not contracted — proposal governs (stone/tile veneer chase, vinyl knee wall, no brick pier)
Brick chimney exterior only, painted to match house
Brick chimney exterior and brick corner pier both contracted

why_it_matters: Brick adds a mason and a pier footing that must be in the slab pour; the proposal prices vinyl knee wall and stone/tile veneer only.

question: What is the existing house wall cladding at the roof tie-in: brick veneer or lap siding?
unblocks: Ledger/beam connection method, siding removal or masonry anchoring tasks, and flashing detail at the tie-in.

choices: Brick veneer (as rendered)
Lap siding (as on the p.5 elevation)
Mixed — brick below, siding above

why_it_matters: Brick veneer requires a through-wall ledger/beam and flashing method different from siding.

question: Is there equipment access to the rear-yard patio area for a mini-excavator or skid steer?
unblocks: Excavation and demo method and duration, and equipment procurement.

choices: Yes — side-yard access clear for a mini-excavator/skid steer
Restricted — gate or fence must be removed first
No — hand excavation and wheelbarrow only

why_it_matters: The breakdown carries a one-day machine rental; no access route means hand excavation and longer demo.

question: Are the painted exposed rafters, ceiling boards, and beadboard wainscot shown in the renders contracted finish work?
unblocks: Whether paint and ceiling/wainscot finish-carpentry tasks are scheduled after framing and before screen install.

choices: Not contracted — bare framing and vinyl knee wall per proposal
Contracted by change order — painted rafters and beadboard wainscot
Painted rafters only, no wainscot

why_it_matters: These add paint and finish-carpentry phases that neither the proposal nor breakdown carries.

question: Do the existing HVAC condenser and downspout at the tie-in corner need to be relocated or rerouted?
unblocks: Whether utility-relocation tasks and an HVAC trade enter the graph ahead of slab and roof framing.

choices: Neither — both stay outside the footprint and roof path
Reroute the downspout only
Relocate the condenser (HVAC sub) and reroute the downspout

why_it_matters: A condenser move adds an HVAC sub and a mechanical permit; a downspout reroute must precede the new roof.

question: Is the roof and screen-wall framing being done by the in-house crew or a framing sub?
unblocks: checklist item framing (Framing (floor, walls, roof structure, sheathing))

choices: In-house crew (3 men)
Framing sub (4-5 men)
In-house roof structure, screen framing by porch/screen sub

why_it_matters: Sub vs in-house sets crew size and duration for the 118-hour roof-structure and enclosure block every later phase waits on.

question: Is there one screen door on the end wall, or also a second door in the outer long wall as the renders show?
unblocks: checklist item exterior_windows_doors (Exterior windows & doors install)

choices: One 3068 screen door on the end wall only
Two doors: end wall plus outer long wall
Undecided — customer still choosing

why_it_matters: Door count changes the screen-bay layout, the door order, and the install day.

question: Has the customer made final selections for the fireplace veneer, hearth surface, and mantel?

choices: Not yet — selections still open
Selected, stock material (~1 week)
Selected, special-order material (~3 weeks)

why_it_matters: Canon bars scheduling before final selections, and these finishes drive the tile/stone order lead time.

question: Who installs the fireplace stone veneer, hearth tile, and mantel — in-house tile setter or a masonry sub?
unblocks: checklist item shower_work (Shower work (waterproofing, tile, grout))

choices: In-house tile setter after the chase is framed
Masonry sub builds chase and veneer together
Fireplace/chimney sub does everything including finish

why_it_matters: The 138-hour fireplace structure/finish block has no checklist home; the trade decides crew, sequence, and how long it runs.

question: Does the wood-burning fireplace and Class A chimney need its own mechanical permit, or does it ride the building permit?

choices: Rides the building permit — no separate mechanical
Separate mechanical/solid-fuel permit required
Unknown — confirm with Johnson City AHJ

why_it_matters: A separate mechanical permit adds an application anchor and an extra inspection before the chase closes.

question: Does the new shed roof get gutters and downspouts, or fascia and trim only?

choices: Fascia and trim only — no gutters
Gutters and downspouts on the new eave
Tie new gutter into the existing downspout system

why_it_matters: Gutters are not itemized anywhere; adding them changes the fascia block duration and material order.

question: Are there any existing vents or penetrations (plumbing, dryer, range) on the rear wall or roof area the new shed roof will cover?
unblocks: checklist item appliance_vent_extension (Extend existing appliance vents through new roof)

choices: None — nothing in the new roof area
One plumbing vent stack
Multiple penetrations (vent stack plus dryer/range exhaust)
Unknown — needs site check

why_it_matters: Each existing penetration under the new roof must be extended and flashed, adding a half-day per item.
